# Architectural illustration

## What

Reusable methods for editable architectural illustrations and invented buildings
when the user requests spatial depth, facade detail or material lighting.

## Why

Spatial and material decisions should remain coherent as details accumulate.
Choosing a suitable representation can reduce repeated derivation and avoidable
reconstruction without prescribing a particular building, camera or style.

## How

Use only the parts relevant to the request. These methods do not apply as a
mandatory pipeline to a flat poster, diagram, icon or deliberately distorted
illustration. User intent and supported tool contracts remain authoritative.
References guide only what they actually show; uncertainty is not measured fact.

### 1. Establish spatial relationships before dense detail

**What:** Choose one consistent spatial model for the requested view. Distinguish
facts supported by references from estimated dimensions and hidden geometry.

**Why:** A detailed facade cannot repair an incorrect attachment, footprint or
front-to-back relationship. Late corrections can invalidate many repeated parts.

**How:** Identify the main mass, attached lower masses, setbacks, roof surfaces and
visible ornament. Record which volumes touch, which surfaces are behind others,
and which top surfaces are visible. Use one unit system and view convention for
connected parts. Resolve the silhouette, attachments and visible overlap before
expanding dense details. Do not invent accurate dimensions from low-resolution
images or add hidden faces merely to make a volume complete. A ready, coherent
part may be drawn immediately; this is not a whole-building pre-draw approval gate.

**Evaluation:** Compare the first usable massing and the final result against the
reference's supported relationships. Count later relationship repairs separately
from deliberately deferred decoration.

### 2. Preserve a consistent projection and explicit visibility order

**What:** Keep world geometry, projected canvas positions and parent-local
coordinates distinct. Keep one camera for connected geometry unless the user
requests a deliberate change.

**Why:** Changing coordinate basis or painter order can produce seams, floating
parts or rear edges appearing through nearer surfaces even with correct vertices.

**How:** Choose a projection appropriate to the requested view; orthographic and
perspective views are different choices. Reuse the chosen projection for connected
surfaces. Signed world coordinates are legitimate; use the consumer's documented
conversion instead of clamping negative values or translating every child
independently. Determine far-to-near order for actual overlapping surfaces.
A single global height sort is not a visibility solution. Split intersecting
surfaces only when their actual visible portions require it. Do not assume the
renderer removes hidden faces or establishes architectural depth automatically.

**Evaluation:** Inspect podium/tower joins, near/far crown edges and top surfaces
at fixed views. Distinguish a geometry error from a layer-order error before
repairing. Do not rebuild geometry when a scoped order correction is sufficient.

### 3. Describe repeated detail as rules when the representation fits

**What:** Represent genuinely repeated geometry with a template and placements;
keep unique or irregular details explicit.

**Why:** Re-deriving and transmitting every repeated vertex increases output and
opportunities for inconsistency without adding design decisions.

**How:** Separate the decisions that vary from those that repeat. Choose one motif,
its dimensions, placement rule, material and visibility order. For a tapered planar
facade, describe a surface and a normalized window/frame motif. For repeated curves,
retain the curve template rather than replacing it with many independently
sampled polygons. Reuse only transformations the selected representation actually
supports; different orientations or topologies may require different templates.
A shared material means intentional linked edits; independent equal colors must
remain independently editable when that is the intent. Do not force an irregular
ornament into a grid or reduce requested detail merely to reduce payload size.

**Evaluation:** Compare required silhouette/detail, editable geometry and paint
order before crediting reduced payload. Track transmitted input bytes and later
repair effort, not generated object count.

### 4. Plan material and lighting relationships across the building

**What:** Treat glass, metal, opaque structure, recesses and cast shadows as
related material decisions under one chosen lighting interpretation.

**Why:** A window grid is not a reflection model. Applying the same bright motif
to every cell or restarting a gradient on every tier can create decorative bands
or checker patterns instead of a coherent facade.

**How:** Establish the large-scale light/dark relationships first. Keep reflections
coherent across a continuous planar facade; change them where orientation,
material or the chosen reflected environment justifies a change. Let mullions,
recesses and structural members remain distinguishable without covering the glass.
Use small highlights only where their scale and material support them. A reference
may support form without supporting lighting; state that uncertainty and choose a
consistent interpretation rather than claiming a physically verified simulation.
Do not create extra scenery/background to justify a reflection.

**Evaluation:** Inspect adjoining tiers and the crown at both overview and detail
scales. Record unintended repetitive bright patterns, abrupt unsupported lighting
resets, and structural elements that obscure required surfaces. Richer color or
more marks alone is not better realism.

## Provenance

Project-authored synthesis of architectural illustration and editable-vector
workflow principles. No external source is quoted. Recorded drawing failures
motivated the topics, but this module contains no case-specific dimensions,
coordinates, object identities, reference answers or required building form.
Effectiveness remains subject to real-agent evaluation.

## Evaluation Guidance

Judge reference-supported spatial relationships, consistent projection, required
editable detail and coherent materials separately. Compare actual correction
scope and transmitted repeated data without using object count as quality.
Retain uncertainty for occluded or underspecified geometry. Fewer operations
are useful only if the requested result and unrelated content are preserved.

# Architectural illustration in Design

## What

Apply relevant architectural methods through existing registered capabilities.

## Why

Design decisions belong to the primary agent; deterministic projection, expansion,
queries and supported checks belong to tools. Avoid re-deriving their results.

## How

This section is Asyra-specific advisory application guidance, not a duplicate API
schema or permission source. The current discovered contract always owns exact
arguments, output identities and recovery. Shared modules contain no Asyra tool
names. Select the representation from the data already available, rather than
reconstructing geometry or retrieving the entire catalog.

| Intent/data already available | Existing consumer | Required handoff and limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Use a reference for massing or a local ornament | validate_reference_images -> select_design_references -> record_design_facts | Validation confirms usable asset evidence, not aesthetic suitability. Primary agent declares exact use/region/limitations and carries returned referenceUses. Derived numbers go to record_design_calculations; neither fact storage nor calculation approves drawing quality. |
| Draw a ready part from chosen world faces | prepare_and_apply_design with projection + projected-face | Choose the camera and geometry once; tool projects supplied geometry and applies canonical parent attachment. No automatic perspective, hidden-face removal or depth ordering. Already projected 2D outlines remain vectors. |
| Expand regular facade detail | Same main tool with surface-grid boundary, normalized motifs, rows/columns and order | Backend owns expansion. Respect the actual four-corner surface contract and cell-major/motif-major semantics. Do not send a list of every projected window corner. |
| Repeat a compatible motif | pattern template + axes, or vector-pattern template + placements | Read exact selected schemas. These are not arbitrary 3D instancing or arbitrary function execution. Confirm supported transformations and split genuinely different motifs. |
| Correct existing local objects | describe_design_apis by known operation -> execute_design_batch with scoped target.query, or retained targets | Bounds plus relevant semantic/ancestor filters identify affected content. Query-bound argument slots are omitted, even empty placeholders. Respect expectedCount failures; do not increase expectedCount blindly. Prefer edits over reconstruction. |
| Correct occlusion | Existing hierarchy.moveElementsRelative operation through batch | Use actual returned element/anchor IDs, preserve geometry, and check intended overlapping region. Save returned outcome before deciding whether a retry may write again. |
| Mechanical check/repair | review_design -> actual mechanicalSelection -> verify_design_checks; repair_design_checks only for supported prescribed-position overflow | No extra model. The repair tool is not an automatic architectural designer, color chooser or general geometry fixer. Unsupported findings return to the primary agent. |
| Visual decision and accumulated results | review_drawing and read_design_checks | Whole-view criterion and local units use separate appropriate evidence. Carry returned bindings/next fields; submit new decisions only for affected units. Capturing images is not recording a pass. Unchanged valid passes remain stored; real shared dependencies may invalidate multiple units. |
| Missing reusable orchestration | Discover existing tools/library first; describe exact contracts; submit_tool -> invoke_tool -> save_tool if needed | Author finite typed recipes only when existing main tools do not cover the work and the steps are genuinely reusable. No JS callbacks, captured request IDs or invented loops. Partial/unknown outcomes stop dependent writes; retry storage alone after successful execution. Do not create a recipe to satisfy an evaluation quota. |

Keep a compact working decision record in existing brief/criteria/fact/check
artifacts: view, units, reference scope, mass relationships, repeated motifs and
remaining defects. This is not a new store or mandatory verbose essay. Use exact
current outputs instead of retransmitting solved geometry. Preserve unaffected
objects and passed decisions. After mutation, inspect affected evidence and an
appropriate final overview; do not reapprove every unrelated part.

## Provenance

App-authored mapping of current Design preparation, construction, review,
operation and tool-library contracts. Exact discovered schemas and returned
receipts own invocation syntax, authority, lifecycle and recovery.

## Evaluation Guidance

Inspect actual intent-to-tool handoffs, rejection reasons, partial recovery,
retained valid judgments and preservation of unrelated content. Check rendered
quality separately; a tool success is not visual acceptance. Do not require a
new composed tool when an existing main tool already covers the task. No
particular building, test result or fixed drawing sequence is prescribed.
